image_description: A group of Australian Pelicans standing on a sandy shore next to a body of blue water. The birds display characteristic white plumage with black flight feathers and pinkish bills. One pelican in the center stands tall, while others are positioned around it, some facing away or partially cropped by the frame edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central pelican clearly displays the signature long bill and the visible outline of the gular pouch beneath the lower mandible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bills are distinctly longer than the heads and exhibit the pale pink/flesh tone typical of Australian Pelicans.

The central pelican exhibits the classic retracted S-curve neck posture.
The tail feathers are short and appear wedge-shaped on the bird in the lower right foreground.
